author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected after the fact. The correction surface shows the visit's current date and description, validates as booking does, updates that visit in place, and returns to the owner's record. Nothing in the interface links to it in this round.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction surface is opened, then that visit's current date and description are shown ready to be changed
given a description and a date later than today, when the correction is submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown
given a pet with a booked visit, when a correction to it succeeds, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again
given an owner's record, when it is opened, then it offers no way to reach the correction surface
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused rather than applied
edge case 4: a visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected without moving its date into the future
non_goals: cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit (NG-5, still out)
any link or button reaching the correction surface — deliberate boundary this round, possible follow-up request
moving a visit to a different pet or owner
correcting anything beyond the visit's date and description
notes: Owner constraints carried verbatim from intake: the correction surface reuses the existing visit form and its visit model attribute, and validates exactly as booking does. NG-5 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; the 2026-08-08 ADR's NG-5 half is marked amended in part. The new ADR still needs an index row in docs/adr/README.md — that file is outside product-requirements-expert write scope. REQ-LANG-002 binds any new user-facing wording to all eleven supported languages, so the narrowest reading introduces none. Three open questions recorded in the PRD rather than blocking: a visible entry point, correcting a visit whose date has passed, and whether the correction form should list the pet's earlier visits. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log, skipped.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The existing owner-aggregate shape covers this with one small adjustment. Owner stays the aggregate root and OwnerRepository.save stays the only write path (system-design.md Overview and the 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' note above Contracts). The correction resolves owner -> pet -> visit through the loaded graph and binds the submitted date and description onto the Visit instance already in pet.getVisits(), so the row updates in place and Pet.addVisit is never called on this path. The adjustment is twofold: VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") method becomes path-aware on an optional visitId, and Pet gains a getVisit(Integer) accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). No new module, repository, template, schema, or message key. Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController are already updated in docs/system-design.md to the contract stated here; the implementation must match them.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit join VisitController; both render pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, POST redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success

loadPetWithVisit gains @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId and serves both the booking and the correction routes; visitId == null keeps today's new-visit branch verbatim, non-null returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and calls no mutator
Pet gains getVisit(Integer) returning null when the id is not among its visits; Visit gains a query answering whether its visit date falls after a supplied reference date
owners.save(owner) cascades the UPDATE through Owner -> Pet -> Visit; no new repository, no schema change, no data.sql change
createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged: the form carries no th:action so it posts to the current URL, and the h2 already drops #{new} when the visit is not new
ownerDetails.html is unchanged; it appears in file_targets only as the subject of the no-link assertion

The loaded graph is detached (spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled, system-design.md Persistence), so a rejected correction leaves the mutated in-memory Visit unpersisted and the save call is the only write

patterns.description: GET .../edit renders the shared create-or-update template, POST .../edit binds onto the entity already loaded in the owner graph and saves through the owner. The visit correction follows this pair exactly; actual path is owner/PetController.java
getPet(Integer) identity lookup over the owned collection, returning null when absent. Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors it, including the null-return contract
not-found refusal by IllegalArgumentException naming only caller-supplied ids. The visit-not-on-this-pet refusal reuses this shape and message form

class-level setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") already covers the new endpoints. It is the mass-assignment control (security-principles.md Realization) that keeps the bound Visit's identity fixed to the one resolved from the path

risks.risk: @ModelAttribute methods run before every handler in the controller. Reusing loadPetWithVisit unchanged on the correction routes would append a placeholder Visit via pet.addVisit and break the same-visit-count criterion
risks.mitigation: Branch loadPetWithVisit on the optional visitId; the correction branch resolves an existing Visit and calls no mutator. Do not split the flow into a second controller class - that would duplicate the owner and pet lookup and split one workflow family across two contracts

risks.risk: Copying the non-future-date check into a second handler puts a second business rule in a web controller. architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog states the recorded deviation does not extend to new rules
risks.mitigation: Move the predicate onto Visit as a query taking the reference date as an argument (no LocalDate.now() inside the entity - principle 3, explicit dependencies). Both POST handlers keep only the result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate") mapping and the existing null-date guard, which is a binding concern rather than a rule. Name the method from the vocabulary (visit date), not from Booking or Appointment. The existing processNewVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture test guards the create path through the move

risks.risk: Reaching for PetValidator as prior art for a VisitValidator. PetController:96 registers it with dataBinder.setValidator, which replaces bean validation; a VisitValidator registered that way would silently drop @NotBlank on Visit.description and break the blank-description criterion
risks.mitigation: Add no Validator in this slice. Bean validation on Visit.description stays as-is and the date rule lives on Visit

risks.risk: Template reuse leaves the submit button reading #{addVisit} on the correction page
risks.mitigation: Accepted this round and recorded, not an oversight. New wording needs a key translated into all eleven bundles under REQ-LANG-002, and no acceptance criterion asks for it. Candidate follow-up request alongside the visible entry point

risks.risk: The booking path sets a hard-coded English flash message ("Your visit has been booked") rather than a message key
risks.mitigation: The correction path adds no flash message; no acceptance criterion requires one. Do not copy the literal - that would compound an existing REQ-LANG-002 breach. Leave the booking path's literal untouched in this slice

risks.risk: VisitControllerTests stubs OwnerRepository with @MockitoBean. testing-principles.md Mocking Policy tolerates the existing usage but asks a new test to prefer a real or hand-written double first
risks.mitigation: test-strategist's call, flagged here rather than resolved silently. The seam is favourable either way: the fixture Owner is the same instance findById returns, so the same-count and unchanged-on-refusal assertions read pet.getVisits() directly with no verify()

risks.risk: No prior art exists for asserting the not-found refusal through MockMvc; the IllegalArgumentException surfaces as a wrapped servlet exception
risks.mitigation: Assert the refusal primarily by the unchanged aggregate - the target visit's date and description unmoved and no save - alongside the propagated IllegalArgumentException. That assertion is the fail-secure property (principle 7) and does not depend on how the exception surfaces

risks.risk: The current VisitControllerTests fixture has no persisted visit, and owner.addPet(pet) is called while the pet is still new
risks.mitigation: The correction tests need a fixture Visit carrying an id inside pet.getVisits(), plus a second pet or a foreign visit id for the wrong-pet criterion

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. --- Item 1 (ADR index row) is DONE by this dispatch, not carried forward: docs/adr/README.md is inside system-design-expert write scope. The 2026-08-28 row is added and the 2026-08-08 row's Status now records the partial amendment, matching the Status line inside that ADR. No implementer action. --- Item 2 (earlier-visits table) decision: change nothing in createOrUpdateVisitForm.html. The premise that the table is suppressed while the visit is new does not hold. Line 51 carries th:if and th:each on the same <tr>, and th:each has the higher Thymeleaf precedence, so the loop variable named visit shadows the model attribute and th:if is evaluated per row against the iterated visit. The predicate is therefore a per-row filter that hides the unsaved placeholder the controller adds via pet.addVisit(new Visit()) - the booking form already lists the pet's persisted visits today. The correction page adds no placeholder, so every persisted visit lists, including the one being corrected. That is the narrowest design-consistent answer: the template is named createOrUpdateVisitForm and its update half has been dormant, the h2 already drops #{new} for a non-new visit, and excluding a visit from its own pet's history would be a new presentation rule that no acceptance criterion carries and that REQ-LANG-002 would drag into wording. Recorded as a decision so a reviewer does not read it as an accident. --- Item 3 (aggregate, lookup, wrong-pet) decision: three parts. (a) Pet.addVisit is not used on the correction path and is not changed; in-place update happens because Spring binds onto the Visit instance already inside pet.getVisits(), and owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE for a row that already has an identity. (b) The lookup is pet.getVisit(visitId) reached as owner.getPet(petId).getVisit(visitId), mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). Outside code still enters through the aggregate root Owner; nothing reaches a Visit without an owner lookup first, and no VisitRepository is introduced. (c) A visitId absent from that pet's visits is refused with IllegalArgumentException from loadPetWithVisit, matching the owner-not-found and pet-not-found refusals two lines above it. The refusal fires before binding and before any mutation, on both GET and POST, so the aggregate is untouched and nothing is saved. The message carries only the caller-supplied ids, no internal detail (security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, error-crossing-out row). A 404 scheme is deliberately not introduced - the codebase has none, and inventing one here would be new ground this slice does not need. --- Trust boundary: the correction endpoints cross the same HTTP-request boundary as the booking endpoints and inherit its controls unchanged - the identifier chain validated through the aggregate, the class-level id disallow list against mass assignment, bean validation plus the date rule before any save, and Thymeleaf's default escaping on redisplay. No new boundary is introduced. --- Carry-forward, not written here: once the date predicate moves onto Visit, architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog's deviation note (which names non-future-visit-date checks as living in controller methods) becomes partly stale. That file is project-owned and outside system-design-expert write scope; flagging it for the human rather than editing it. --- Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, VisitController (REQ-VIS-003 mapping, plus the Visit row's purpose corrected off the vocabulary's rejected term 'appointment'); docs/adr/README.md index row. No new ADR: the product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, and the design adds no hard-to-reverse choice or catalog departure warranting one.

findings.description: The future-date validation block `if (visit.getDate() != null && !visit.isDatedAfter(LocalDate.now())) { result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate"); }` is now duplicated verbatim between `processNewVisitForm` and the new `processVisitCorrectionForm`. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Tenancy/IDOR: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:70-97) resolves owner -> pet -> visit strictly through the loaded aggregate. owner.getPet(petId) (Owner.java:117) walks only that owner's pets and pet.getVisit(visitId) (Pet.java:91) walks only that pet's visits, so a visitId belonging to another owner's pet, or to another pet of the same owner, resolves to null and is refused with IllegalArgumentException at VisitController.java:88 before any binding or save. Because the method is the shared @ModelAttribute, the refusal runs on GET (VisitController.java:113) and POST (VisitController.java:140) alike - no verb reaches the handler with an unresolved visit. Confirmed no cross-owner mutation path.

Mass assignment: the @InitBinder at VisitController.java:53-56 keeps the project-wide disallow list ("id", "*.id"), matching OwnerController.java:61 and PetController.java:91/97 - swept all four binder configurations, none omits it. Visit exposes only date and description (Visit.java:38-43) and holds no pet back-reference, so the correction POST cannot rebind visit.id or re-parent the visit to another pet; the bound instance is the one already inside pet.getVisits(), so the save updates in place rather than adding a row.

Information disclosure: the refusal message at VisitController.java:88 echoes only the two identifiers the caller already supplied and is worded identically whether the visit does not exist at all or belongs to a record the caller may not see - no existence oracle. It mirrors the neighbouring owner/pet refusals (VisitController.java:74, PetController.java:70). The redisplayed form on a validation error renders only the resolved pet's own visits (templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html) and leaks nothing about other records.

XSS: description and date are redisplayed through the escaping inputField fragment and th:text; no th:utext or escaping bypass exists anywhere under src/main/resources/templates. The correction path introduces no new sink.

CSRF posture is identical to the pre-existing visit-creation POST and owner-edit POST - no Spring Security, no CSRF token, on any route. Per docs/security-principles.md this is the recorded demonstration baseline; the slice adds one mutating endpoint on an already fully open surface (correction of a visit the caller can already create and whose owner record it can already edit unauthenticated), so blast radius is not widened and no authz regression is introduced. The endpoint is declared in docs/system-design.md:97.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only), so no dependency was added, upgraded, or repointed; no new CVE surface to check. Note: IntelliJ MCP was unreachable in this environment, so no IDE inspection oracle was consulted - findings come from native reads and greps only.

Observation, not a finding: processVisitCorrectionForm (VisitController.java:141) takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner, so request parameters bind onto the Owner before owners.save. This is the identical shape of the pre-existing processNewVisitForm (VisitController.java:121) and of OwnerController's edit POST, is guarded by the same id disallow list, and grants no capability an unauthenticated caller lacks today - recorded for visibility, not raised as a defect of this slice.

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid: 'A slice that lifts a rule into a unit exercisable without framework context adds a unit test.' This slice lifted the non-future-date rule into Visit.isDatedAfter and added Pet.getVisit — both pure logic, no I/O, no Spring context needed. Neither has a direct unit test; both are exercised only indirectly by booting the full MockMvc web layer in VisitControllerTests (no PetTests.java or VisitTests.java exists in src/test/java/.../owner/). Line coverage is satisfied incidentally, but the pyramid ratio the brief targets (~80% unit, ~15% integration) moves the wrong direction: a new pure-logic rule added a web-layer test instead of retiring one.
findings.fix: Add a small VisitTests.java covering isDatedAfter (date after reference -> true; date equal to reference -> false; date before reference -> false) and extend/add a PetTests.java covering getVisit (existing visit id -> returns it; unknown id -> null; id belonging to a still-new/unsaved visit -> null per the isNew() guard). These are pure unit tests, no @WebMvcTest needed.

approved_aspects: Same-visit-count criterion is explicitly asserted, not implied: theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddASecondVisitToThePet uses assertThat(pet.getVisits()).containsExactly(bookedVisit) after the POST, which fails if a bug added a second Visit or swapped the instance

theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlace asserts on the same bookedVisit object reference the pet already held pre-POST, so it fails for the right reason if the controller mistakenly created a new Visit instead of binding onto the existing one

theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoLinkToTheVisitCorrectionForm can fail for the right reason: it asserts the page contains the /visits/new link (proving the visits section actually rendered) before asserting doesNotContainPattern on /visits/\d+/edit, and ownerDetails.html genuinely emits no edit-visit anchor, so the assertion is a real absence check, not a vacuous one against an unrendered page

theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet covers both GET and POST verbs per the design's before-binding guard, and asserts no mutation occurred and owners.save was never invoked

All new/modified tests use factory methods (createAnOwnerWithOnePet, createABookedVisit) instead of raw constructors, and all meaningful data (dates, descriptions, ids) is named per the three-tier convention with no mystery literals

Mocking stays within policy: OwnerRepository is the sole mock (a system-boundary I/O dependency, consistent with the pre-existing suite convention), and all domain objects (Owner, Pet, Visit) are real instances
